name: Cursor
summary: An AI code editor (a VS Code fork) whose built-in agent edits, searches and runs commands in your repo, with the same agent also available as a terminal CLI and as cloud agents running in remote VMs.

status.d: Cursor announced on 2026-08-14 that it has been acquired by SpaceX, after an April 2026 partnership with SpaceXAI; the product continues and now ships its own Grok models.

first_release.d: Not stated on any page fetched today; web search budget was exhausted.

latest.v: changelog entry: Rollouts and Security Review

open.d: Closed source commercial editor, CLI and cloud service; no licence or repository is offered on the docs or pricing pages.

models.v: own Grok 4.x and Composer 2.5, plus Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Z.ai, Moonshot, Meta
models.d: Cursor lists its own model families (Grok 4.5 to 4.7, jointly trained with SpaceXAI, and Composer 2.5) beside vendor models; a Cursor Router picks a model per task. The models page mentions BYOK usage only in passing.

loop.v: agent loop with Agent/Plan/Ask modes, subagents, /goal, Projects
loop.d: Built-in subagents Explore, Bash and Browser keep noisy output out of the main context; custom subagents can run in parallel in separate git worktrees or cloud VMs. Projects (2026-09-10) add a coordinator agent delegating to subagents; /goal pursues long-lived objectives.

edit.d: The tools page names an Edit files tool that applies edits automatically; the overview describes a search-and-replace approach. Whether a separate apply model still runs is not stated on the fetched pages (unconfirmed). Checkpoints allow rollback.

context.v: .cursor/rules (.mdc), AGENTS.md, user and team rules; Instant Grep local index
context.d: Rules live in .cursor/rules as .mdc files (Always, Intelligently, by glob, manually) or nested AGENTS.md files; team rules come from the dashboard. Search now uses Instant Grep, a local index, and Cursor says it does not store embeddings of your codebase for search.

perms.v: Auto-review / Allowlist / Run Everything; Seatbelt and Landlock+seccomp sandbox
perms.d: Run modes: Auto-review (allowlisted calls run, other shell commands sandboxed, the rest judged by a classifier steered by permissions.json), Allowlist and Run Everything. Sandbox: Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) on macOS, Landlock plus seccomp on Linux with bubblewrap fallback; sandbox.json sets network and path policy. Cloud agents run in isolated VMs.

ext.v: MCP (mcp.json), hooks.json, plugins marketplace, skills, custom modes
ext.d: MCP over stdio, SSE and streamable HTTP with one-click marketplace installs; hooks.json with events such as preToolUse, beforeShellExecution, preCompact and stop; custom modes are pinned skills. Subagent files are also read from .claude/agents and .codex/agents.

where.v: editor, CLI (agent), web, mobile, Slack, GitHub, Linear, API
where.d: Cloud agents start from cursor.com/agents, desktop, iOS and Android apps, Slack, GitHub or Bitbucket PR comments, Linear and an API; self-hosted machines since 2026-09-02. The CLI command is agent with a print mode (-p) for scripts and CI.

price.v: Hobby free, Individual $20/mo, Teams $40/user/mo, Enterprise custom
price.d: As of 2026-10-05: Hobby (limited Agent requests, Composer), Individual $20/mo (extended Agent limits, generous Grok limits, frontier models, cloud agents, Bugbot on usage billing), Teams $40/user/mo (Bugbot reviews, SSO), Enterprise (pooled usage, SCIM, model and MCP controls). Cloud agents bill at API rates.

notes: Cursor was acquired by SpaceX on 2026-08-14; its own Grok 4.6 (2026-08-12) and Grok 4.7 (2026-09-21) models now headline the model list and the pricing page (src: https://cursor.com/blog/joining-spacex).

Correction to a common belief: Cursor's docs now say it does not store embeddings of your codebase for search; search runs on Instant Grep, an index built on your machine (src: https://cursor.com/docs/context/codebase-indexing).
Bugbot (PR review bot) is included on Teams and on usage billing for Individual; 2026-09-23 added Rollouts and Security Review bots (src: https://cursor.com/changelog).
Cursor reads subagent definitions from .claude/agents and .codex/agents as well as .cursor/agents, a sign of convergence between harness file formats (src: https://cursor.com/docs/context/subagents).

name: Windsurf (now Devin Desktop)
maker: Cognition (acquired from the Windsurf/Codeium team, July 2025)
summary: A VS Code based agentic editor, originally built by Codeium around its Cascade agent, which Cognition bought in July 2025 and renamed Devin Desktop in June 2026; its agent is now Devin Local, the same harness as the Devin CLI.

status.d: Cognition signed a deal to acquire Windsurf on 2025-07-14. On 2026-06-02 (v3.0.12) Windsurf became Devin Desktop; on 2026-09-08 (v3.9.19) Cascade was removed and Devin Local became the only agent. windsurf.com/pricing and /changelog now redirect to devin.ai and docs.devin.ai. The product is still sold and updated (v3.10.48, 2026-09-29), but no longer under the Windsurf name or with Cascade.

first_release.d: The Devin Desktop changelog fetched today starts at v2.0.67 (2026-04-22); the original Windsurf launch date was not on any page fetched.

open.d: Closed source commercial editor; the docs offer installers only, no source.

models.v: Cognition SWE models plus Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and open models
models.d: Devin Local (shared with Devin CLI) offers Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Cognition models (SWE-1.6, SWE-1.7, SWE-2) plus DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM, with Adaptive routing and Fusion lead/sidekick pairing. ChatGPT plans can be linked so GPT usage bills to ChatGPT.

loop.v: Devin Local agent; Agent Command Center over local, worktree and cloud agents
loop.d: Devin Local has plan mode and foreground or background subagents; the Agent Command Center (Kanban style, Spaces) manages local, worktree and Devin Cloud agents and third party ACP agents side by side. Cascade (removed 2026-09-08) had Code/Chat modes and Arena mode.

edit.v: unconfirmed: edit and write tools (Devin Local)
edit.d: Devin Local shares the Devin CLI tool set, whose permission table names edit and write tools; the edit format (exact replace vs patch) is not documented on the pages fetched.

context.v: AGENTS.md, .devin/rules, legacy .windsurf/rules and .windsurfrules; RAG index; Fast Context
context.d: Rules from AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/*.md, .windsurf/rules and .windsurfrules; a RAG-based context engine indexes the codebase and Fast Context is a retrieval subagent using SWE-grep models. Cascade's auto-generated memories (~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/) apply to legacy Cascade only; Devin Local does not persist them and a wizard migrates them to skills.

perms.v: Devin CLI permission modes and OS sandbox
perms.d: Devin Local uses the CLI modes (Normal, Accept Edits, Smart, Bypass, Autonomous) with allow/deny rules and an optional OS sandbox (bubblewrap plus socat on Linux; not supported on Windows). The macOS sandbox mechanism is not named on the page fetched.

ext.v: MCP, hooks, skills, plugins, workflows, ACP agents
ext.d: MCP servers (legacy Cascade used mcp_config.json), hooks, SKILL.md skills in .devin/skills, Cascade workflows as markdown, Open VSX extensions, and third party agents via the Agent Client Protocol.

where.v: desktop editor on macOS, Windows, Linux; hands off to Devin Cloud
where.d: Desktop editor; legacy Windsurf plugins still exist for JetBrains, VS Code, Vim and others; sessions can run Local, in a Worktree or in Devin Cloud.

price.v: Devin plans: Free, Pro $20, Max $200, Teams $80/mo min + $40 per full seat, Enterprise
price.d: As of 2026-10-05 windsurf.com/pricing redirects to devin.ai/pricing; one quota covers Devin sessions, Devin CLI and Devin Desktop. Pro includes free SWE-2 use in Desktop and CLI through 2026-10-16; Teams flex seats do not include Desktop.

notes: Relevance: Windsurf as a brand is effectively gone. Its editor lives on as Devin Desktop, and its Cascade agent was removed on 2026-09-08 in favour of Devin Local (the Devin CLI harness), which Cognition says uses up to 30% fewer tokens (src: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/devin-local).
Acquisition terms per Cognition (2025-07-14): product, IP, trademark and team; Windsurf had $82M ARR and 350+ enterprise customers (src: https://cognition.com/blog/windsurf).
Devin CLI and Devin Desktop read legacy .windsurfrules and .windsurf/rules, so old Windsurf repos keep working (src: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/rules).

sources_read.what: Devin Desktop (Windsurf) release notes, rename and Cascade removal

name: Devin
summary: An autonomous AI software engineer that works in its own cloud VM (shell, editor, browser) on tickets you assign from the web, Slack or an issue tracker and returns pull requests; since 2026 it also ships as a local terminal agent (Devin CLI) and as the agent inside Devin Desktop.

status.d: Cognition crossed $1B annualized revenue run rate (2026-09-25) and raised a Series E ($2B at $48B, 2026-09-08).

first_release.d: The earliest Devin release note fetched is dated 2024-05-13; the original launch announcement was not fetched.

open.d: Closed source hosted service and CLI binary.

models.v: Cognition SWE models plus Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM
models.d: Devin CLI supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Cognition models and open models; Adaptive is a router and Fusion pairs a frontier lead with a cheap sidekick (for example SWE-2). A ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan can be linked to pay for GPT usage; otherwise usage draws from the Devin quota.

loop.v: async cloud sessions; CLI subagents; parallel managed sessions
loop.d: Cloud sessions run asynchronously; Devin can orchestrate managed sessions in parallel, and Dynamic Workflows fan sessions out from a Python script. The CLI has foreground and background subagents (run_subagent, profiles subagent_explore and subagent_general), and /handoff moves work between local and cloud.

edit.v: unconfirmed: edit and write tools (CLI); IDE and shell in cloud VM
edit.d: The CLI permission table names edit and write tools but not their format; cloud sessions expose an IDE, Shell and Browser that log all code edits.

context.v: AGENTS.md (16 KiB injected), Memory drive, DeepWiki, Ask Devin, Skills, Knowledge (deprecated)
context.d: AGENTS.md is injected up to 16 KiB; the CLI also reads .devin/rules, .windsurfrules and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Memory is a personal git repo of markdown notes with MEMORY.md loaded each session and Dreaming to tidy it. DeepWiki generates repo wikis and Ask Devin answers code questions from an index. Knowledge is deprecated and migrating to Skills in plugins. Hooks include PostCompaction.

perms.v: cloud VM per session; CLI modes Normal, Accept Edits, Smart, Bypass, Autonomous
perms.d: Cloud sessions run in VMs (Linux, also macOS and Windows VMs) restricted by Security Profiles; Outposts run them on your own machines. CLI: allow/deny/ask rules plus modes; Autonomous pairs with --sandbox (bubblewrap plus socat on Linux, fail-closed, unsupported on Windows); Smart lets a fast model approve safe actions.

ext.v: MCP marketplace, hooks, plugins, skills, playbooks, slash commands, REST API, Devin MCP
ext.d: Playbooks are shared reusable prompts; SKILL.md skills; plugins bundle skills, rules, hooks and MCP servers; CLI hooks (PreToolUse, Stop, SessionStart...) also pick up .claude hooks; the REST API uses service users; the Devin MCP server lets other agents drive sessions.

where.v: web app, Slack, Teams, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, Linear, Jira, CLI, Devin Desktop, ACP in JetBrains/Zed/Xcode
where.d: Sessions start from app.devin.ai, Slack, Microsoft Teams, PR comments, Linear and Jira, automations on schedules and webhooks, the API, the CLI (devin --cloud) or Devin Desktop; the CLI also runs inside JetBrains, Zed and Xcode via ACP.

price.v: Free, Pro $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Teams $80/mo min + $40/full seat, Enterprise (ACUs)
price.d: As of 2026-10-05: self-serve plans use daily and weekly quotas shared across cloud sessions, CLI and Desktop, with on-demand credits beyond; Enterprise consumes Agent Compute Units (ACUs) against an order form.

notes: Devin is no longer cloud only: Devin CLI is a local terminal agent (macOS, Linux, WSL, Windows) with cloud handoff, and since 2026-09-21 it can run and SSH into cloud sessions (src: https://docs.devin.ai/cli/changelog/stable).

Self-serve pricing moved from ACUs to quotas (Free, Pro, Max, Teams) in April 2026 per Cognition's blog index; ACUs remain for Enterprise (src: https://cognition.com/blog, https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/usage).

Fusion (2026-09-11): a frontier lead model delegates to a cheap sidekick; Cognition claims up to 39% better efficiency and argues for price per task, not per token (src: https://cognition.com/blog/local-fusion).
Devin Wiki is now DeepWiki and Devin Search is now Ask Devin; Knowledge is deprecated in favour of Skills (src: https://docs.devin.ai/llms.txt).

name: Cline
summary: An open source coding agent that started as a VS Code extension (originally called Claude Dev) and now also ships as a CLI/TUI, a desktop app and a TypeScript SDK, using whatever model provider and API key you bring.

status.d: Repo pushed 2026-10-05; extension v4.x now runs on the SDK backed harness, and some older features (Focus Chain todo list, Explain Changes, .clineignore) are deprecated.

first_release.d: CHANGELOG lists 0.0.6 as 'Initial release' of the extension, then named Claude Dev; GitHub repo created 2024-07-06.

latest.v: extension v4.1.22; CLI cli-v3.0.68; SDK v0.0.90; Desktop v0.0.43

open.d: GitHub reports Apache License 2.0 for cline/cline; the enterprise layer (SSO, RBAC, dashboards) is a paid add-on.

models.v: any provider, BYO key, local models, or Cline provider at cost
models.d: Anthropic (API key or Claude Code subscription), OpenAI (key or Codex OAuth), Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, DeepSeek, Qwen, Z AI, OpenRouter, OpenAI compatible, 30+ more, and local Ollama or LM Studio; or the Cline usage billing provider and ClinePass.

loop.v: Plan & Act modes, subagents, Kanban parallel agents, CLI agent teams
loop.d: Plan mode explores without changing files, Act mode executes. Subagents run parallel read-only research; Kanban runs multiple agents in isolated git worktrees; CLI Agent Teams coordinate several agents. The Focus Chain todo list was deprecated.

edit.d: Current SDK/ClineCore tools: editor (view and edit files), apply_patch (apply unified diffs), read_files, search (ripgrep), bash. Older docs name XML tools replace_in_file (SEARCH/REPLACE blocks) and write_to_file. Checkpoints roll back file changes while keeping the chat.

context.v: .clinerules/ or .cline/rules/, AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules; Memory Bank; Auto Compact
context.d: Rules from .clinerules/ or .cline/rules/ (frontmatter scoping), AGENTS.md and ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, and auto-detected .cursorrules and .windsurfrules. Memory Bank is a methodology (markdown files kept by a rule), not a built-in store. Auto Compact summarizes near the context limit. Cline does no codebase indexing.

perms.v: per-tool approval, Auto Approve categories, YOLO mode; no OS sandbox
perms.d: Every tool call asks unless Auto Approve allows its category (read, edit, safe commands, all commands, browser, MCP); YOLO mode approves everything. No OS sandbox is documented; the docs advise using isolated environments.

ext.v: MCP (with marketplace), hooks, plugins, skills, slash commands, SDK
ext.d: MCP servers via ~/.cline/mcp.json and the MCP Marketplace; plugins add tools and hooks (documented under the SDK); SKILL.md style skills; the @cline/core SDK embeds the harness; ACP lets Zed, JetBrains, Neovim and Emacs host Cline.

where.v: VS Code, JetBrains (Enterprise), CLI/TUI, Desktop, ACP editors, GitHub Actions, chat connectors
where.d: Runs on your machine; CLI samples include GitHub Actions PR review; CLI connectors reach Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat and WhatsApp; Desktop can drive a remote box over SSH.

price.v: free and BYO key; Cline provider at cost; ClinePass $9.99/mo; Enterprise custom
price.d: As of 2026-10-05: Open Source plan free (extension, CLI, inference at cost or BYOK, MCP Marketplace); Enterprise custom (JetBrains, SSO, RBAC, provider limits). ClinePass is an optional $9.99/mo subscription giving 2-5x usage on open coding models.

notes: Cline has been rebuilt on an SDK backed architecture (packages @cline/core, @cline/agents, @cline/llms); the extension is now at v4.x, and the edit tool is apply_patch with unified diffs rather than the old replace_in_file SEARCH/REPLACE blocks (src: https://docs.cline.bot/tools-reference/all-cline-tools).
Cline removed .clineignore because it never stopped shell access and gave a false sense of security; a deprecations page now tracks this (src: https://docs.cline.bot/resources/deprecations).
The product was first released as Claude Dev (src: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cline/cline/main/CHANGELOG.md).

name: Roo Code
summary: A VS Code extension forked from Cline that added role-based modes (Code, Architect, Ask, Debug, Orchestrator) so one agent could plan, code and delegate subtasks; it was shut down in May 2026 when its team moved to Roomote, a self-hostable cloud agent.

status.d: The VS Code Marketplace page says 'The Roo Code Extension was shut down on May 15th' and points users to ZooCode or Cline. The GitHub repo is archived (last push and last release v3.54.0 on 2026-05-15). The 3.53.0 changelog says the original team is going all in on Roomote and a community team would carry the plugin forward. roocode.com now redirects to roomote.dev.

first_release.d: The CHANGELOG's oldest entry is 2.1.2 (adds .clinerules support, inherited from the Cline fork); the RooCodeInc repo was created 2024-10-31. No dated first release was found.

open.d: GitHub reports Apache-2.0; the repo is now archived (read only). Roomote, the successor, reports no standard licence (NOASSERTION) and is free to self-host up to 10 users.

models.d: Late releases added providers and models such as Poe, xAI Grok 4.20 via the Responses API, OpenAI GPT-5.4 mini/nano and GPT-5.5 via the Codex provider, Claude Opus 4.7 on Vertex.

loop.v: modes: Code, Ask, Architect, Debug, Orchestrator (Boomerang); new_task subtasks; update_todo_list
loop.d: Each mode limits tool groups (Ask: read and mcp; Architect: edit only markdown). Orchestrator mode splits work into subtasks run in other modes via new_task, each returning a summary (Boomerang Tasks, later renamed Task Orchestration). Custom modes live in .roomodes.

edit.d: The tool list includes apply_diff (search/replace blocks), apply_patch, search_replace, edit, edit_file and write_to_file. Checkpoints keep a shadow git repo of the workspace.

context.v: .roo/rules and .roo/rules-{mode}, AGENTS.md; Qdrant embedding index; context condensing
context.d: Rules in ~/.roo/rules/ and workspace .roo/rules/ with per-mode rules-{modeSlug}. Optional Codebase Indexing parses code with Tree-sitter, embeds blocks and stores vectors in Qdrant for the codebase_search tool. Intelligent Context Condensing summarizes long chats.

perms.d: Every action prompts unless enabled in the Auto-Approve dropdown; the docs warn that command auto-approval is dangerous. No OS sandbox is documented.

ext.v: MCP, Roo Code Marketplace, custom modes, slash commands, skills
ext.d: MCP servers (use_mcp_tool, access_mcp_resource), a marketplace of modes and MCP servers, slash commands and skills.

where.d: VS Code extension only; the team's cloud work continues as Roomote, which runs in your own infrastructure and works from Slack, Teams, Discord, GitHub and GitLab.

price.v: free extension with your own key (discontinued)
price.d: As of 2026-10-05 there is no Roo Code plan; Roomote Cloud costs $49/mo up to 10 users, $249/mo for 11 to 50, $499/mo for 51 to 100; self-hosted free up to 10 users.

notes: Roo Code is discontinued: shut down 2026-05-15 per the Marketplace page, GitHub repo archived; the team now builds Roomote (src: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=RooVeterinaryInc.roo-cline, https://roomote.dev/).
The Marketplace page shows version 3.54.0 with a 'released' date of 2026-09-28, while GitHub dates v3.54.0 to 2026-05-15; the GitHub date is used here.

Its idea that lasts: modes as tool-restricted personas, and an Orchestrator that delegates to subtasks and receives a summary back (Boomerang), an early form of subagents (src: https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/basic-usage/using-modes).

name: Kilo Code
summary: An open source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal, with a pay-as-you-go model gateway and cloud agents; it absorbed Roo Code style modes and its CLI is a fork of OpenCode.

status.d: Included because it is large and active in October 2026 (MIT repo with about 27.5k stars, pushed 2026-10-05, Anaconda cites 3M+ developers) and is where many Roo Code users went. Anaconda announced the acquisition on 2026-07-15; Kilo stays available and open source.

first_release.d: GitHub repo created 2025-03-10; no dated first release fetched.

open.d: GitHub reports MIT; Anaconda describes the codebase as open source and source-available.

models.v: 500+ models via Kilo Gateway, BYOK, local
models.d: Kilo Gateway is pay-as-you-go over 500+ models from 60+ providers; BYOK and local models (for example Anaconda Desktop, Ollama) also work.

loop.v: Code, Plan, Debug agents with native subagents; cloud agents
loop.d: Orchestrator mode is deprecated because agents with full tool access (Code, Plan, Debug) now delegate to subagents natively; cloud agents and Gas Town run in the cloud.

edit.d: The edit tool format was not confirmed on pages fetched today.

context.v: AGENTS.md, .kilo/rules, opt-in project Memory, codebase indexing
context.d: AGENTS.md replaces the deprecated Memory Bank (.kilo/rules/memory-bank/); Kilo Memory is opt-in and project scoped; codebase indexing uses embeddings (e.g. gemini-embedding-001).

perms.v: auto-approve settings; optional OS sandbox (macOS, Linux)
perms.d: Sandbox is off by default; when on it limits writes and by default blocks outbound network, configured in kilo.jsonc; not available on Windows and fails closed. The sandbox technology is not named on the page.

ext.v: MCP, plugins (OpenCode style), skills, custom subagents, custom rules
ext.d: MCP in the extension and CLI; plugins and custom tools follow OpenCode conventions (opencode.json, .kilo/tool/).

where.v: VS Code, JetBrains, CLI, cloud agents, code review
where.d: Extensions for VS Code and JetBrains, CLI via npm, Homebrew and curl, plus cloud agents and a code review agent.

price.v: Free; Teams $15/user/mo; Enterprise custom; Gateway pay as you go; Kilo Pass $19 to $199/mo
price.d: As of 2026-10-05: free extensions and CLI with free models or BYOK; Gateway usage with no subscription; Kilo Pass adds up to 50% bonus credits; cloud compute billed per second ($0.33 to $1.20/hour).

notes: Anaconda acquired Kilo Code (announced 2026-07-15) (src: https://www.anaconda.com/blog/anaconda-acquires-kilo-code).
Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode, per the README (src: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/main/README.md).

sources_read.what: full docs incl. sandboxing, AGENTS.md, memory, orchestrator

name: Kiro
summary: AWS's agentic coding platform built around spec-driven development (requirements, design, tasks) and steering files, with one agent harness shared by an IDE, a CLI, a web app with cloud sessions, a mobile app and Kiro Crew.

status.d: Included because it is AWS's flagship coding agent and is shipping weekly in October 2026 (IDE 1.2 and CLI 2.26 on 2026-09-30, CLI 2.27.0 on 2026-10-01).

first_release.d: The public issue tracker repo was created 2025-06-17; no dated first release fetched.

open.d: The GitHub repo is only an issue and feedback tracker; the README says the product source is not hosted there.

models.v: Auto router plus Claude, GPT and open weight models
models.d: Default Auto routing; selectable Claude Opus 5 and 5.5, Sonnet 5 and 5.5, GPT-5.6, DeepSeek 3.2, Qwen3 Coder Next; each model has a credit multiplier.

loop.v: specs, Autopilot, subagents, workflows, cloud sessions
loop.d: Specs turn a prompt into requirements, design and tasks; the IDE has Autopilot; subagents run in parallel with isolated context; workflows run multi-step plans, on Web in background cloud sessions.

edit.d: The permission capabilities name fs_write (create or edit files); the edit format was not documented on pages fetched.

context.d: Steering markdown in .kiro/steering/ (workspace) and ~/.kiro/steering/ (global) with inclusion modes; AGENTS.md is supported on every surface; automatic compaction summarizes history; powers load context and MCP servers on demand.

perms.v: capability-based permissions (deny > ask > allow); Web runs in a cloud sandbox
perms.d: permissions.yaml rules per capability (fs_read, fs_write, shell, web_fetch, mcp, subagent...) with effects deny, ask, allow, replacing the older trusted commands and denylist. On Web the agent runs in an isolated cloud sandbox instead of prompting; local OS sandbox not confirmed.

ext.v: MCP, hooks, powers, skills, custom agents, ACP
ext.d: Hooks on file changes, tool use or task completion; powers follow the Agent Plugins specification; custom agents; saved prompts as slash commands; works in ACP-compatible IDEs.

where.v: IDE, CLI, Web, Mobile (iOS preview), Crew, ACP IDEs
where.d: One harness and one .kiro/ config across all surfaces; cloud sessions can be started or attached from any surface.

price.v: Free 50 credits; Pro $20; Pro+ $40; Pro Max $100; Power $200 per user/mo
price.d: As of 2026-10-05: credits of 1,000 / 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 on paid tiers; extra credits $0.04 each; cloud sessions use credits with no separate compute charge.

notes: Kiro's lasting idea is spec-driven development: the agent writes requirements, a design and a task list before code (src: https://kiro.dev/docs/).

Kiro docs describe a CLI 3.0 with plan mode and capability permissions, while the changelog's newest CLI release is 2.27.0 (2026-10-01); 3.0 may be a preview (src: https://kiro.dev/llms.txt, https://kiro.dev/changelog/).
